Make a shape collage.

Little scraps become something wonderful.

Ages 3–825 minIndoors

A scrap of paper can become a roof, a hill or a completely imaginary creature. This open-ended project starts with simple shapes and leaves room for children to decide what their picture will become.

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

Gather your bits.

Tick things off as you get ready.

A note for grown-ups

Supervise cutting and gluing. Use clean paper without staples or sharp edges. Keep small scraps and glue out of mouths; tear larger shapes for younger children.

A little more guidance ↗
ONE STEP AT A TIME

Let's make it happen.

  1. Gather a small palette

    Choose three or four paper colours. Look for differences in texture, such as a smooth wrapper and a rough paper bag.

  2. Make your shapes

    Tear or cut several large shapes. Try a long strip, a rounded shape and a triangle. Exact shapes are not important.

  3. Try before you glue

    Move the pieces around your background. Can a triangle become a mountain? What happens when one shape overlaps another? Try two arrangements.

  4. Build the picture

    Glue the background shapes first, then add the smaller pieces on top. Press each piece down gently.

  5. Add your last marks

    Use crayons to add lines or details. Give your collage a title and tell someone about one choice you made.

THE LITTLE BIT OF LEARNING

What's happening here?

Moving shapes before sticking them down gives children a chance to plan and revise. Overlapping creates layers, while different colours and textures help parts of a picture stand out.

Keep the wondering going.

  • Which shape did you use in an unexpected way?
  • What looks near, and what looks far away?
  • How would your picture change with one colour removed?

Make it work for you.

Keep it simple

Offer a few large, pre-torn shapes. Let the child place them and narrate the picture while an adult helps with glue.

Take it further

Limit the palette to three colours and show distance using overlapping shapes. Try another version with the same pieces.

Not quite going to plan?

Paper curling? Use less glue and let the collage dry flat. If choosing a picture feels difficult, start with an abstract arrangement of colours.
